qt: to the Commission Nina Carberry (PPE) Subject:

The current Erasmus+ Regulation (2021–2027) explicitly provides funding for not-for-profit European sport events, supporting initiatives such as the European Sport for All Games, the Special Olympics and other events promoting inclusion, grassroots participation and volunteering. However, the proposed Erasmus+ Regulation for 2028–2034 no longer identifies these events as a standalone funding action, raising concerns about the continuation of this support. Can the Commission clarify whether funding for the organisation of not-for-profit European sport events will continue under Erasmus+ 2028–2034, including through the proposed partnerships for cooperation or sport collaborative alliances, and whether a dedicated funding mechanism will be maintained?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.11.2026) The Commission intends to continue funding not-for-profit European sport events under Erasmus+ 2028-2034. Article 7(a) of the Commission’s proposal for a Regulation establishing Erasmus+ for the period 2028–2034 (pending adoption by the Council and the European Parliament) provides that ‘the Programme shall support experimentation, preparation and implementation of the Union’s policy agendas and tools covering skills, education and training, youth and sport’1. Although not-for-profit European sport events are not explicitly mentioned in the Regulation, the Commission considers that the support for not-for-profit European sport events falls within the scope of the general provision set out in the above-mentioned article. The Commission intends to maintain a dedicated funding mechanism to support these events.
